text:
Jonathan Castagna came to Calgary as part of the March trade that sent MacKenzie Weegar to Utah, signed after his junior season at Cornell, and needed five shifts of his NHL debut on Oct 8 to record an assist. Seventeen games in, the 21-year-old from Toronto has 3 assists, no goals and a regular spot centering the bottom of the lineup, at about 12 minutes a night.

The early numbers are what you'd expect from a rookie in a checking role. He has 1.44 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and no goals yet, which is mostly bad luck in a small sample; our range has him somewhere between 3 and 11 goals by season's end. At five on five Calgary has had 44.2% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about 4 points worse than without him, and he's thrown 31 hits. His last college season, 34 points in 34 games and the ECAC's best defensive forward award, translates to roughly 33 points over 82 NHL games by our league translation. The first NHL goal is the obvious milestone; the five-on-five share is the one that keeps him in the lineup.
headline: Castagna is learning the job on Calgary's fourth line
